summary:
Rio de Janeiro recorded only 3 trans killings in 2025 (a low rate of ~0.18/million against a population of ~17 M), well below the national average. However, two distinct visitor-facing signals pull the score modestly below the national 0.71: a documented extortion pattern in Niterói and a tourist-targeting scam in Copacabana.

In January–February 2026, multiple trans sex workers in central Niterói reported a two-year coercive regime: a man claiming militia and public-agent connections forced them to pay R$120 per week each and had 'almost strangled three of the girls.' The alleged extorter was an ex-employee of Niterói city hall, arrested in 'Operação Ronda Sumbria' by the 76ª DP, and remanded in pre-trial custody. The institutional response was mixed—arrests and dismissal occurred, but the racket operated under the appearance of state backing for roughly two years before intervention. Trans council member Benny Briolly brought the case to the Public Ministry.

Separately, in Copacabana the tourist police (Deat) arrested two trans women caught extorting a Norwegian tourist with threats to circulate intimate videos—a documented, visitor-facing scam vector. The killing rate is low, but the coercive pattern with state implication and the tourist-targeting scam justify a deviation of about 0.03 below national. Compared with São Paulo (no deviation), Rio's risk is qualitative rather than numerical.

Extra (Rio police desk, Feb 2026): the state court (TJRJ) decreed pre-trial custody of a man accused of exploiting travestis and trans women in central Niterói as a pimp; he had been a Niterói city-hall employee until dismissed in January 2026, after a complaint the trans city councillor Benny Briolly took to the Public Ministry.

Super Rádio Tupi (4 Apr 2025): tourist-police delegates (Deat) arrested two trans women in flagrante at a Copacabana hotel extorting a Norwegian tourist - posing as sex workers, then threatening to circulate secretly filmed intimate videos unless paid; the victim had already transferred about R$35,000, and one arrested woman had prior record for extortion, criminal association and pimping.

SBT News report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th edition of the ANTRA dossier: Brazil recorded 80 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, down 34% on 2024, still the world's highest; state counts for 2025 - Ceará and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7, Goiás/Maranhão/Pará 5, Paraíba, Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo 4 each, Mato Grosso and Rio de Janeiro 3, Alagoas, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul 2; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (~140/yr); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% committed outside state capitals.
